comparator.name: Molecular Life Sciences
comparator.academicYear: 2026–2027 formally adopted Faculty of Science EER, standard 180-EC route
comparator.route: Molecular Life Sciences, ordinary route with neutral first-listed 18-EC ML1 selection
comparator.sourceNotes: Articles 7.3–7.5 of the adopted 2026–27 English EER establish 60 EC of first-year compulsory molecular and chemistry courses, 45 EC of later compulsory courses, 57 EC of differentiation with at least 18 EC from the ML1 list, a 12-EC supervised Bachelor’s Internship and Report as the final project, and 6 EC genuine free electives: 60+45+57+12+6=180. Academic Skills first-year (0 EC) and RADAr do not add credits. Three first-listed 6-EC ML1 options instantiate the 18-EC minimum without implying these particular courses are mandatory for every student. The remaining 39 EC is restricted to eligible science/medical-science bachelor courses and potentially a permitted minor; it is not filled with invented named modules. Panorama A and the English molecular philosophy instance are neutral formal choices. The prospective year-three page lists multiple 60-EC subject menus and a mandatory internship, but these illustrative lists are not stacked and do not override the adopted EER. The 2026–27 EER excludes specific overlapping Biology/Chemistry courses and three named minors; none is treated as freely interchangeable.

components.note: The remaining 39 EC of the 57-EC differentiation phase is selected under Article 7.4: additional ML1 options, approved NWI/MED bachelor courses, and optionally an accessible coherent minor (normally 15–30 EC). This is restricted programme choice, not 39 EC of unrestricted free electives. The three first-listed ML1 courses above are one neutral 18-EC instance, not chosen to optimise UCR fit.

routeSelection.route: Molecular Life Sciences, ordinary route with neutral first-listed 18-EC ML1 selection
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English-taught Molecular Life Sciences bachelor, not one optional year-three thematic menu or an educational minor. The adopted EER specifies one shared core and a flexible differentiation phase. The first three ML1 items are neutral first-listed choices solely to instantiate the 18-EC minimum; the other 39 EC remains accurately represented as restricted selection.

programmes.label: Molecular Life Sciences at Radboud University

exception.reason: The Radboud degree is an integrated molecular biology AND chemistry programme. Its compulsory first year already includes atoms and molecules, analytical chemistry and a chemical-analysis lab, organic chemistry and synthesis lab, biochemistry and its lab, thermodynamics, cell biophysics and a molecular-sciences lab. The later compulsory core deepens organic, inorganic and analytical chemistry, crystal structure, biomolecular mechanisms and structural bioinformatics, then requires a supervised 12-EC research internship. UCR offers valuable molecular-cell and biomedical courses but lacks a sequence in organic/inorganic/analytical/physical chemistry, molecular spectroscopy and synthesis, and has only one broad life-science laboratory course. A 24-course UCR schedule could sustain biomedical biology with data methods, but it would omit the defining chemistry and multi-lab spine and would misrepresent equivalence to this molecular-science degree.
exception.curriculumContext: The current adopted 2026–27 Faculty of Science EER, rather than the loosely grouped prospective year-three thematic examples, controls the 180-EC reconstruction. Its differentiation phase is restricted and its research internship is mandatory. The exception follows assessment of the closest 24-course molecular/biomedical possibility against the entire current UCR enriched course database.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Read all 151 current enriched UCR course rows with descriptions, profiles, semester availability and prerequisites. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory, HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics and HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity cover genuine biological and biomedical parts. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science and BENGATE102 Research Methods & Statistics can support quantitative work. HCBLIFE214 introduces biochemical and molecular lab techniques, but no available courses provide the formally required analytical-chemistry lab, organic synthesis laboratories, physical chemistry/thermodynamics, spectroscopy or a sustained organic/inorganic chemistry progression. The only feasible alternative would be a different biomedical/data curriculum, so no 24-course closest UCR degree is encoded.
